#### SOCIO RELIGIOUS REFORMS

Young Bengal Movement (Late 1820s and Early 1830s)

  • Started by: Henry Vivian Derozio.
  • He was a teacher at the Hindu College.

Dharma Sabha → Revitalist Movement (1830)

  • It was started by Radhakanta Deb → He was against the idea of Brahmo Samaj.

**Paramhansa Mandali (1849) → (\\SSC considers this year as 1840)**

  • It was formed by Dadoba Pandurang and Durgaram Mehtaji in Maharashtra.

Prarthana Samaj (1867)

  • It was formed by Atmaram Pandurang in Maharashtra.
  • M.G. Ranade joined it in 1870, R G Bhandarkar was also a member.

Deoband Movement (1866)

  • Started by: Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi.
  • Launched in: Saharanpur district in Uttar Pradesh.

Singh Sabha Movement (1873)

  • It started in Amritsar.
  • It aimed to revive Sikh faith by bringing back the converts (led by Khem Singh Bedi and others).

Satyasodhak Samaj (1873)

  • It was formed by Jyotiba Phule (he was from Mali/Gardener community) in Maharashtra against caste discrimination.
  • In 1848, Jyotiba Phule along with his wife Savitri Phule (first female teacher of India) started the first school for girls in Pune.
  • Books written by Jyotiba Phule: Gulamgiri, Sarvajanik Satyadharma (both in Marathi).

Arya Samaj (1875)

  • It was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati (original name: Mool Shankar).
  • First unit of Arya Samaj was opened at Bombay and later shifted to Lahore.
  • He advocated for Caste less and Class less society.
  • He gave slogans "Go Back to Vedas" and "India for Indians".
  • He considered Vedas as infallible but criticised Puranas.
  • He believed in Karma and Reincarnation.
  • He subscribed (support) the Chaturvarna system on the basis of work not by birth.
  • He was against the Idol Worship.
  • Book written by him: Satyarth Prakash.
  • 1886: Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) College in Lahore was established in memory of Swami Dayanand by Mahatma Hansraj.
  • 1893: The Arya Samaj members in Punjab were divided on the question of vegetarianism and modern education. The group that refrained from eating meat were called the "Mahatma" group and the other group, the "Cultured Party".

Aligarh Movement (1875)

  • Started by: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
  • He established a Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College in 1875 which was later called Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
  • He also founded Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.

Dev Samaj (1887)

  • Founder: Shiv Narayan Agnihotri at Lahore.

Shuddhi Movement

  • It was a purification movement started by Arya Samaj for Christian converters to bring back to Hinduism.

Swami Vivekananda

  • He started the Ramkrishna Movement.
  • Original Name: Narendranath Dutta.
  • His birth: 12 Jan 1863 is celebrated as "National Youth Day".
  • Died on: 4 July 1902.
  • He believed in idol worship.
  • Books written: Raja Yoga, Karma Yoga.
  • 1893: Swami Vivekananda gave a speech in Chicago (USA) in a conference.
  • He advocated on how to make balance between Materialism and Spiritualism.
  • Swami Vivekananda Rock Memorial is in Tamil Nadu (Kanyakumari).

Ramkrishna Mission / Ramkrishna Movement (1897)

  • It was started by Swami Vivekananda in the memory of his Guru Ramkrishna Paramhansa (Priest of Kali Mandir in Calcutta) → Original name: Gadadhar Chattopadhyay.
  • HQ: Belur Math; Howrah (West Bengal).
  • According to him "Service to man is service to God".

Balshashtri Jambhekar

  • He started two newspapers: Darpan and Digdarshan.
  • He is remembered as the "Father of Marathi Journalism".

Gopal Hari Deshmukh

  • Pen name: Lokhitwadi.
  • He started weekly newspapers: Prabhakar and Hitechhu.

Gopal Ganesh Agarkar

  • He started a weekly: Sudharak.

Servants of India Society (1905)

  • Founder: Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
  • He was political Guru of Gandhi and Jinnah.

Seva Sadan (1908)

  • Founder: B. M. Malabari.
  • He worked against child marriage and for widow remarriage.

Social Service League (1911)

  • Founder: Narayana Malhar Joshi at Bombay.

#### SOCIO RELIGIOUS REFORMS

  • He also started All India Trade Union Congress in 1920.

Faraizi Movement (1818)

  • Started by: Haji Shariatullah.

Wahabi Movement

  • Started by: Sayyid Ahmad Bareivi of Rae Bareli.

#### SOCIO RELIGIOUS REFORM MOVEMENTS IN SOUTH INDIA

Satnami Movement

  • It started in 1820s in Chhatisgarh region by Guru Ghasidas who belonged to Satnami sect.
  • He worked with the leatherworkers in 1870.

Theosophical Society (1875)

  • It was started in New York (USA) by HP Blavatsky and HS Olcott.
  • The society's HQ was shifted to Adyar Madras from New York in 1882.
  • Later Annie Besant took its membership.
  • This society was highly influenced by Hindu belief system.

Indian National Social Conference (1887)

  • Founders: M. G. Ranade and Raghunath Rao.
  • Pledge Movement was started by them against child marriage.

Shree Narayana Guru Dharmam Paripalana (SNDP) Movement

  • Started by: Shree Narayan Guru Swami for the upliftment of Ezhavas Community of Kerala.
  • Important slogan: "Oru Jathi, Oru Matham, Oru Daivam" (One Caste, One Religion, One God for All).
Stri Purush Tulna was written by: Tarabai Shinde.

Justice Movement (1917)

  • Started by: C. N. Mudaliar, T. M. Nair and P. Tyagaraja.

Self Respect Movement (1925)

  • Founder: E. V Ramaswamy Naicker (also known as Periyar).

Temple Entry Movement (for the entry of Dalits in temple)

  • In North India (1930), it was started by B. R. Ambedkar.
  • In South India (1924), it was started by T. K. Madhavan.
  • Vaikom Satyagraha (1924), it was started by T. K. Madhavan, K. P. Kesava Menon, and K. Kelappan in Travancore (Kerala).
  • B. R. Ambedkar started Temple Entry Movement in 1930 here for the entry of Dalits in this temple.
